location: NIST Handbook 135 (2020), printed page 29 / PDF page 61, section 3.2.2.1, equation 3-7
text: Uniform amounts have the same dollar value from year to year. The uniform present value factor, when multiplied by the annually recurring cost, yields the present value of the entire stream of costs over the designated number of years. Equation 3-7 (mathematical transcription): PV = A0 * ((1 + d)^t - 1) / (d * (1 + d)^t). A0 is the annually recurring uniform amount, d the annual discount rate, and t the number of years. The example uses an annual maintenance cost of $100 over 5 years with a 3% discount rate and gives PV = $457.97. The transcription was checked against PDF text on 2026-10-29; it retains the source notation, not canonical program symbols.
